metadata.title: OECD Reviews of Evaluation and Assessment in Education: Bosnia and Herzegovina (EN)
metadata.venue: OECD Reviews of Evaluation and Assessment in Education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD review chapter does not conduct a student-level statistical analysis with an analytic sample drawn from PISA/TIMSS microdata; instead, it synthesises policy and system-level evidence about assessment and evaluation practices in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As a result, there are no survey weights to apply (e.g., no W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) and no replicate-weight variance estimation (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is performed. Where the chapter references international assessments (PISA 2018; TIMSS 2019/Grade 8; and earlier participation), it uses them as benchmarks in a descriptive policy context rather than re-estimating weighted achievement models. For any future empirical work using PISA/TIMSS microdata, analysts should apply the official complex survey weights provided in the international database and use the corresponding replicate weights when variance estimation is required.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a policy review and does not estimate student-level cognitive outcomes using PV-based achievement scores; therefore, plausible values handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is also not reported because no microdata model fitting or imputation/deletion procedure is performed in the chapter.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is constructed. The chapter synthesises system-level information about assessment policies and practices across Bosnia and Herzegovina’s administrative units, and it references international assessment participation (PISA 2018; TIMSS 2019) as contextual benchmarks rather than analysing microdata.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD review chapter analyses how Bosnia and Herzegovina’s education system uses (or does not use) assessment and evaluation mechanisms to support learning, equity, and system improvement. It describes the country’s limited participation in international large-scale assessments (PISA 2018 and TIMSS 2019/Grade 8 and earlier TIMSS participation), and it contrasts this with the lack of state-level standardised testing and the fragmentation of assessment rulebooks across entities, cantons, and districts. The chapter documents that classroom assessment is largely summative and norm-based, formative assessment is inconsistently defined, and teachers often lack assessment literacy support (e.g., moderation, exemplars, and guidance). It also outlines policy pathways for strengthening assessment value (rulebook revisions, feedback practices, diagnostic assessments, and teacher training) and for improving external examinations and system evaluation capacity. No predictive modelling, PV estimation, or weighted statistical inference is conducted in this chapter.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse for empirical-ML fields because the document is an OECD policy review rather than an original quantitative study. It does not report an analytic student sample, model training/evaluation, or PV/missing-data procedures; instead, it provides qualitative synthesis and policy recommendations grounded in international assessment participation and system documentation. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country Ns, and main_findings for ML targets are intentionally empty.
